items.title: Regularization Permits First Formal Contracts for Thousands
items.body: Guillermo, Germán, and Alessia are among thousands who signed their first formal employment contracts this July after receiving provisional regularization permits. The extraordinary process allows undocumented migrants to leave the underground economy, contribute to Social Security, and access better labor conditions. Tens of thousands are now paying into the system, although some employers remain cautious pending final approval. Many had previously worked 11-hour days for €800 a month without legal protections.

items.title: Spain Faces France in World Cup Semifinal
items.body: Spain's national football team meets France in the World Cup semifinal on July 14, 2026, at 21:00. La Roja advanced after eliminating Portugal in Dallas and Belgium in Los Angeles. The Spanish Football Federation has invited all La Liga clubs to support the team in the semifinal and potential final. The high-stakes match is expected to bring celebrations and affect public life across the country.

items.title: Household Real Estate Wealth Hits €7.73 Trillion
items.body: The value of real estate owned by Spanish households climbed to €7.73 trillion in 2025, a 13% increase from 2024. Foreign buyers accounted for €12,049.4 million in transactions, with 92% involving second-hand homes and just 8% new builds. The growth in household property wealth has been uninterrupted since 2014, accelerating in the past two years. Rising values continue to shape affordability for all residents, including those looking to purchase homes.

items.title: Congress Advances Pension Bridge for Self-Employed Mutualists
items.body: Self-employed professionals, such as architects, lawyers, and doctors, who belong to mutual societies may soon transfer their contributions to Social Security to secure a minimum pension. The government estimates the measure will cost €5,204 million and initially benefit around 47,000 mutualistas, although some sources say hundreds of thousands could be eligible. Congress is close to approving the law, addressing long-standing complaints about extremely low pensions for these autónomos (self-employed). For many, the reform would guarantee a basic retirement income.

items.title: Heat Wave Drives Record Death Toll
items.body: Spain has recorded 1,682 heat-attributable deaths since May 1, with 622 occurring in just the first nine days of July. A second scorching wave between July 6 and 10 caused most of those, while an earlier wave killed 278. June 2026 was the deadliest June from heat since 2017, and May's toll surpassed the previous five Mays combined. The relentless heat is overwhelming hospitals and endangering the elderly in particular.

items.title: Tax Advisor Warns Missed Deductions Boosted State Revenue
items.body: Spain's 2025 income tax campaign collected a record €10.6 billion, nearly double the previous year's amount, partly because many taxpayers failed to claim eligible deductions, according to tax advisor José Ramón López Martínez. He notes that some individuals also did not file at all, even when they were owed a refund. The oversight means many residents overpaid their taxes unknowingly, highlighting the need for better awareness of available breaks.

items.title: Law Requires Total Price in Real Estate Ads
items.body: Economist José María Páez confirms that Law 10/2025, in effect since December 2025, now mandates that property advertisements display the total purchase price, including all fees, from the first listing. The rule aims to prevent buyers from encountering hidden costs after showing interest. Previously, many only learned of extra charges later, a practice now illegal. The transparency measure offers important protection for anyone navigating the Spanish property market.

items.title: EU Funds Lift GDP Per Capita Just 0.2% Over Five Years
items.body: An EY report reveals that after five years of Next Generation EU funds, Spain's GDP per capita has risen by just 0.2%, while private investment remains 3.3% below 2019 levels. The government had projected that €140 billion in public funds would unlock €500 billion in private investment, but that multiplier has not materialized. The disappointing results raise questions about the effectiveness of the recovery plan for the country's long-term growth.

items.title: Gibraltar Border Fence to Be Removed in Three Days
items.body: The metal fence separating Gibraltar and Spain since the Franco era will be dismantled on July 15, 2026. Originally erected in 1969 when the border was closed, the barrier remained even after the crossing reopened. Its removal promises smoother movement for thousands who commute daily between the two territories. The change follows recent political agreements and marks a new chapter for the Campo de Gibraltar region.

items.title: Seven NATO Allies Rescue A400M Program in Seville
items.body: Seven NATO countries—Belgium, Croatia, France, Poland, Spain, Turkey, and the UK—will jointly own and operate a fleet of A400M aircraft, ensuring the program continues at Airbus's Seville plant. The factory had already dismantled two of its four assembly hangars, anticipating the project would end after 2028. The agreement, announced at the NATO Defense Industry Forum in Ankara, safeguards local jobs and a key aerospace hub.

items.title: 131 Migrants Rescued from Listing Boat Near El Hierro
items.body: Salvamento Marítimo rescued 131 people from a heavily listing cayuco off El Hierro after it was spotted by Guardia Civil radar on the morning of July 11. Seven survivors were hospitalized; they reported having had no food or water for the final two days of the journey. The incident adds to ongoing migration pressure in the Canary Islands, where such arrivals strain local resources and integration services.
